title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
description: The software constructs all or part of an SQL command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended SQL command when it is sent to a downstream database engine.
remediation: Use parameterized queries (prepared statements) with bound typed parameters for all database access. Avoid string concatenation, string interpolation, or raw formatting of user-controlled input into query strings.
snippet: PreparedStatement stmt = conn.prepareStatement("SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = ?"); stmt.setString(1, username);

title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
description: The software constructs an OS command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended OS command when it is sent for system execution.
remediation: Avoid invoking shell interpreters (e.g. system(), exec(), popen(), runtime.exec("sh -c ...")). If executing external processes is necessary, pass arguments as a strict, fixed argument array without shell interpolation.
snippet: ProcessBuilder pb = new ProcessBuilder("ping", "-c", "1", targetHost); pb.start();

title: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
description: The software contains hard-coded credentials, such as passwords, API keys, private cryptographic keys, or JWT signing secrets, within the source code or configuration files.
remediation: Externalize sensitive secrets to secure environment variables, encrypted secrets managers (e.g., HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager), or container secrets. Never commit plaintext tokens to version control.
snippet: String dbPass = System.getenv("DB_PASSWORD"); String jwtSecret = System.getenv("JWT_SECRET");

title: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
description: The use of a broken or risky cryptographic algorithm, such as MD5, SHA1, DES, or RC4 for password hashing or integrity verification, which makes data vulnerable to collision attacks, preimage attacks, or rapid brute forcing.
remediation: Use modern, cryptographically robust algorithms: Argon2id, bcrypt, or PBKDF2 with SHA-256 for password hashing; AES-GCM (256-bit) or ChaCha20-Poly1305 for symmetric encryption; SHA-256 or SHA-3 for digital signatures.

title: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
description: The software does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users, allowing arbitrary JavaScript execution in client browsers.
remediation: Contextually encode user-supplied data before rendering it in HTML, JavaScript, CSS, or URL contexts (e.g., OWASP Java Encoder). Implement a strict Content Security Policy (CSP).

title: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
description: The software uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize sequences such as '..' that can resolve to a location outside of the restricted directory.
remediation: Validate input against an allowlist of valid file paths. Normalize paths using canonical path APIs and verify that the target path begins with the intended base directory.
snippet: Path target = baseDir.resolve(filename).normalize(); if (!target.startsWith(baseDir)) { throw new SecurityException(); }

title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
description: The web application does not, or can not, verify that a well-formed, valid, consistent request was intentionally provided by the user who submitted the request.
remediation: Implement anti-CSRF synchronizer tokens for all state-changing HTTP operations (POST, PUT, DELETE). Use SameSite=Strict or SameSite=Lax cookie attributes.

title: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
description: The software allows the attacker to upload or transfer files of dangerous types that can be directly processed or executed within the server environment (e.g., .php, .jsp, .exe, .sh).
remediation: Validate file extensions and MIME types against a strict whitelist. Store uploaded files outside the web document root, generate unique random filenames, and enforce antivirus/sandbox scanning.
snippet: if (!ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS.contains(ext)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid file type");

title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
description: The application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution, denial of service, or authentication bypass.
remediation: Avoid native Java ObjectInputStream serialization or unsafe deserialization libraries (e.g., Python pickle, YAML unsafe load). Use safe serialization formats such as JSON with strict schema validation.

title: Improper Authentication
description: When an actor claims to have a given identity, the software does not prove or insufficiently proves that the claim is correct.
remediation: Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA), secure password storage with salt and work factors, rate limiting on login attempts, and robust session management.

title: Missing Authorization
description: The software does not perform an authorization check when an actor attempts to access a resource or perform an action.
remediation: Enforce role-based (RBAC) or attribute-based access control (ABAC) at the server layer for every API endpoint and business function. Adopt a deny-by-default posture.

title: Incorrect Authorization
description: The software performs an authorization check when an actor attempts to access a resource or perform an action, but does not correctly enforce the authorization rules.
remediation: Verify tenant ownership and object-level permissions on every database lookup (preventing Insecure Direct Object References - IDOR).

title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
description: The web server receives a URL or similar request from an upstream component and retrieves the contents of this specified URL, but it does not sufficiently ensure that the request is being sent to the expected destination.
remediation: Validate target URLs against a strict domain whitelist. Disallow private IP ranges (127.0.0.0/8, 10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.0.0/16, 169.254.169.254) and internal hostnames.
snippet: InetAddress addr = InetAddress.getByName(uri.getHost()); if (addr.isSiteLocalAddress() || addr.isLoopbackAddress()) throw new SecurityException();

title: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
description: The software constructs all or part of a code segment using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the syntax or behavior of the intended code segment (e.g., eval(), eval-like functions).
remediation: Do not pass dynamic input into dynamic evaluation functions (eval(), Function(), ScriptEngine). Use static data structures or domain-specific expression parsers with restricted AST capabilities.
snippet:
// Avoid eval(userInput); parse structured JSON instead:
DataObj obj = objectMapper.readValue(jsonInput, DataObj.class);

title: Improper Input Validation
description: The product receives input or data, but does not validate or incorrectly validates that the input has the properties that are required to process the data safely and correctly.
remediation: Validate all incoming data using strict whitelist patterns, type checks, length constraints, and bounded ranges at the API entry point.

title: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
description: The software does not properly control the allocation and maintenance of a limited resource, thereby enabling an actor to influence the amount of resources consumed (CPU, memory, disk, network sockets).
remediation: Implement rate limiting, maximum request body size limits, pagination on query results, and strict timeouts on background execution.

title: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
description: The software transmits sensitive data, such as passwords, API keys, personal identification numbers, or session tokens, in cleartext across a communications channel.
remediation: Enforce TLS 1.3/1.2 on all transport endpoints. Set HSTS headers and require secure cookie flags (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite).

title: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
description: The product exposes sensitive information (e.g. stack traces, system paths, internal IPs, configuration variables) to an actor who is not explicitly authorized to have access to that information.
remediation: Use generic error responses for end users. Sanitize exception messages and avoid returning database or framework stack traces in HTTP responses.
snippet: @ExceptionHandler(Exception.class) public ResponseEntity<?> handleGenericError() { return ResponseEntity.status(500).body("An unexpected error occurred."); }

title: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')
description: The software concurrently executes code paths that access a shared resource (such as bank balances, inventory counts, or file locks) without adequate synchronization mechanisms (TOCTOU).
remediation: Use atomic primitives, transactional isolation levels (SELECT FOR UPDATE / serializable), distributed locks, or synchronized blocks.

title: Incorrect Default Permissions
description: During installation or execution, the software sets default permissions for resources (files, sockets, database accounts) that are more permissive than necessary (e.g., world-readable, world-writable files 0777).
remediation: Apply the principle of least privilege. Set file permissions explicitly to 0600 or 0700 for sensitive configuration files and private keys.

title: OWASP Top 10 - A01:2021 Broken Access Control
description: Access control enforces policy such that users cannot act outside of their intended permissions. Failures typically lead to unauthorized information disclosure, modification, or destruction of all data or performing a business function outside the user's limits.
remediation: Enforce access controls in trusted server-side code or serverless API. Deny access by default, implement access control mechanisms once and re-use them throughout the application.

title: OWASP Top 10 - A02:2021 Cryptographic Failures
description: Failures related to cryptography (or lack thereof), which often leads to sensitive data exposure or system compromise. This includes cleartext transmission, weak algorithms, default keys, and missing encryption at rest.
remediation: Classify data processed, stored, or transmitted by an application. Apply strong standard encryption algorithms, ciphers, and keys; ensure proper key management.

title: OWASP Top 10 - A03:2021 Injection
description: An application is vulnerable to attack when user-supplied data is not validated, filtered, or sanitized by the application, or dynamic queries or commands are executed directly in the interpreter.
remediation: Use safe APIs that avoid the interpreter entirely or provide a parameterized interface. Use positive or whitelist input validation and SQL LIMIT / other query controls.
snippet: jdbcTemplate.query("SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE id = ?", rowMapper, accountId);

title: OWASP Top 10 - A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration
description: The application or server is configured with default accounts, unneeded features enabled, overly permissive CORS, missing security headers, or unpatched flaws.
remediation: Establish a secure installation and configuration hardening process. Keep all platforms and dependencies up to date with automated dependency auditing.

title: OWASP Top 10 - A07:2021 Identification and Authentication Failures
description: Confirmation of the user's identity, authentication, and session management is critical to protect against authentication-related attacks such as credential stuffing and brute force.
remediation: Implement multi-factor authentication, do not ship with default credentials, implement weak password checks, align password length/complexity with NIST 800-63b.
